title: Comments of Buckeye Power, Inc. on PJM Interconnection L.L.C.'s 10/13/2026 filing under ER27-126.

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                      BEFORE THE
                        FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


        PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                               Docket No. ER27-126-000


                           COMMENTS OF BUCKEYE POWER, INC.

           Pursuant to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”)

October 14, 2026, Combined Notice of Filings #1, 1 Buckeye Power, Inc. (“Buckeye”) 2

respectfully submits these limited comments on the October 13, 2026, filing by PJM

Interconnection L.L.C. (“PJM”) in the above-captioned proceeding. 3 PJM’s Filing

includes an executed “Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of Ohio’s State

Agreement Approach Request,” 4 filed pursuant to (1) Federal Power Act (“FPA”)

section 205 5 and (2) Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C. (“Operating Agreement”), Schedule 6, section 1.5.9 (the “State

Agreement Approach” or “SAA”).

           The SAA “provides a formal mechanism by which PJM’s regional transmission

expansion planning (“RTEP”) process can respond to a request from one or more states

that PJM develop transmission facilities that would assist them in implementing their

public policy initiatives.” 6 Here, the Ohio Federal Energy Advocate (“Ohio FEA”) has

invoked the SAA process for “an integrated artificial intelligence (“AI”) data center,

generation, and transmission development centered at and around the former United

States Department of Energy (“DOE”) Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike

County, Ohio,” with roughly 10,000 megawatts (“MW”) each of new load and new

generation that requires three proposed 765 kilovolt (“kV”) transmission lines and

related infrastructure. 7

            Importantly, the Filing states that the data center customer, SB Energy, “has

committed to funding required infrastructure through arrangements designed to protect

other customers, supporting grid resilience, and investing in local employment,

workforce development, community benefits, and site remediation.” 8 Similar, the Ohio

SAA Request itself confirms that “SB Energy will pay for that infrastructure so that Ohio

customers are protected from the costs.” 9 Buckeye files these Comments to express

support for this commitment that SB Energy will pay for the infrastructure identified in

the Study Agreement (i.e., the “Required Transmission Upgrades” 10), consistent with the

Ohio SAA Request and SB Energy’s commitment that this project “be fully consistent

with the Ratepayer Protection Pledge.” 11

         Buckeye recognizes that PJM and the other Parties to the Study Agreement intend

to make future filing(s) to address cost allocation under Commission-jurisdictional

rates. 12 Such future filing(s) will establish the details of the cost recovery mechanisms

needed to ensure that, ultimately, these costs are borne by SB Energy and not other Ohio

customers. But given the significant risk of cost shifting posed by the Ohio SAA Request

at issue, the Commission should condition any acceptance of the Study Agreement on

future cost allocation filing(s) implementing the Parties’ intent that these costs are

ultimately borne by SB Energy. As explained below, this means that no costs should be

allocated to wholesale customers such as Buckeye that are not able to suballocate those

costs to SB Energy.

                                         COMMENTS

I.       BACKGROUND ON THE FILING

         As noted in this Filing, the Ohio FEA and PJM seek to use the SAA process to

develop transmission facilities to accommodate an integrated artificial intelligence data

center of approximately 9,570 MW coupled with 10,170 MW of gross new generation

(the “Project”). Buckeye understands that the Project will receive retail distribution

service from Ohio Power Company (“Ohio Power”), 13 and AEP Ohio Transmission

Company, Inc. (“AEP Ohio”) will provide transmission service and make the


12
   Buckeye reserves all rights with respect to such future filing(s). As a transmission dependent utility,
Buckeye is subject to PJM’s Open Access Transmission Tariff, which includes cost recovery for
transmission upgrades and expansions made by each transmission owner in Ohio and regional transmission
projects assigned by PJM. Accordingly, the rates Buckeye pays for PJM transmission service could be
adversely affected by the significant transmission infrastructure contemplated under the Study Agreement.
It is therefore essential that the transmission facilities and upgrades PJM identifies through the Study
Agreement are allocated in a way that implements the Parties’ intent that SB Energy is ultimately the entity
solely responsible for those costs, and that the other wholesale transmission customers, like Buckeye and its
members, are not potentially saddled with those costs.
 See Filing, Transmittal Letter at 2 (stating that the initial load will be “served under Ohio Power
13

Company’s . . . Data Center Tariff” (citation omitted)).
                                                 -4-


transmission investments necessary to serve the Project. 14 The Project is anticipated to

require significant transmission investments, including three 765 kV transmission lines

and related infrastructure. 15

            The Filing states that “SB Energy has committed to structuring and developing

[the Project] to be fully consistent with the Ratepayer Protection Pledge,” and to “funding

required infrastructure through arrangements designed to protect other customers,

supporting grid resilience, and investing in local employment, workforce development,

community benefits, and site remediation.” 16 This commitment is reflected in the Study

Agreement, which notes that one of SB Energy’s affiliates “has committed to bear all

costs of transmission facilities and associated infrastructure needed to reliably

interconnect [the Project].” 17 It is also reflected in the Ohio FEA’s SAA Request, which

states that “SB Energy will pay for that infrastructure so that Ohio customers are

protected from the costs.” 18 In furtherance of this commitment, the Ohio FEA has

requested use of the SAA process to “ensure that costs associated with the transmission

lines and associated infrastructure constructed by AEP Ohio or its designee are assigned

to Ohio to then be further allocated to SB Energy, which has committed to pay the

costs.” 19




 Id. at 6 (explaining that AEP Ohio would construct the transmission infrastructure needed under the Ohio
14

SAA Request).

            The Filing before the Commission in this proceeding presents the Study

Agreement for the Project. According to the Filing, PJM will make a future filing with

the Commission to address the cost allocation methodology for the Project, and PJM

intends to work with SB Energy and AEP Ohio to develop that methodology in parallel

with the study process under the Study Agreement. 20 Specifically, cost allocation will

have to be addressed in an FPA section 205 filing to amend Schedule 12 – Appendix C of

the PJM Tariff, which addresses the “the assignment of cost responsibility of State

Agreement Public Policy Projects constructed in accordance with Operating Agreement,

Schedule 6, section 1.5.9 among Responsible Customers.” 21 The Filing states that

additional proceedings before the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (“PUCO”) will

also be needed “to ensure that the costs associated with the transmission lines and related

infrastructure necessary to interconnect and serve the [Project] are assigned to Ohio and

then further allocated to SB Energy.” 22

II.         COMMISSION ACTION IN THIS PROCEEDING SHOULD BE
            CONDITIONED ON IMPLEMENTATION OF SB ENERGY’S
            COMMITMENT TO PAY FOR THE TRANSMISSION
            INVESTMENT REQUIRED TO SERVE THE PROJECT.

            Buckeye supports the intent of the SAA Request and Study Agreement to ensure

that SB Energy will pay for the Required Transmission Upgrades associated with the

Project. The commitments in the filing are particularly important given the very

significant transmission investment required to accommodate the new load and



20
     Filing, Transmittal Letter at 17.
21
  PJM Tariff, Sched. 12 – App. C. See also PPL Elec. Utils. Corp., 181 FERC ¶ 61,178, P 3 (2022) (“A
State Agreement Public Policy Project must have a Commission-accepted cost allocation method to permit
recovery of the project’s costs.”).
22
     Filing, Transmittal Letter at 17.
                                                -6-


generation at the Project, and the risk that other customers might bear those increased

costs absent such commitments.

           Buckeye recognizes that the Study Agreement itself does not establish a cost

allocation methodology and instead states that this issue will be addressed in a future

Commission proceeding. Given the magnitude of potential costs and the significant risk

of cost shifting, however, the Commission should condition any acceptance of the Study

Report on future cost allocation filing(s) being consistent with the explicit intent that SB

Energy ultimately bear the costs of the Required Transmission Upgrades. At minimum,

the Commission should expressly recognize the Parties’ intent that SB Energy—not other

customers—bear these costs. Buckeye reserves all rights with respect to such future

proceeding(s) to address cost allocation.

           In addition, Buckeye highlights that the Parties’ intent to have SB Energy bear the

costs of the Required Transmission Upgrades has implications for the proper way to

allocate costs through Commission-jurisdictional rates. As stated in the Ohio SAA

Request, the intent is to “ensure that costs associated with the transmission lines and

associated infrastructure constructed by AEP Ohio or its designee are assigned to Ohio to

then be further allocated to SB Energy, which has committed to pay the costs.” 23 It is

therefore essential that costs be allocated, for purposes of Commission-jurisdictional

rates, in a manner that then allows Ohio to further allocate all such costs to SB Energy,

consistent with SB Energy’s commitment to pay for them.

           Accordingly, no Required Transmission Upgrade costs should be allocated to

wholesale transmission customers like Buckeye and its members. Buckeye and its


23
     Ohio SAA Request at 2 (emphasis added).
                                                  -7-


members have no contractual relationship with SB Energy, and SB Energy is not a retail

customer of Buckeye or its members. Any costs allocated to Buckeye through

Commission-jurisdictional rates therefore cannot then be further suballocated to SB

Energy through retail rates. 24 For example, if Commission-jurisdictional transmission

rates allocate such costs to every Ohio wholesale transmission customer, or every

wholesale transmission customer of AEP Ohio, then wholesale transmission customers

like Buckeye cannot then further suballocate their shares of costs to SB Energy. 25 That

outcome is contrary to the fundamental premise of the Ohio SAA Request and Study

Agreement—that SB Energy’s will pay for the transmission costs required for the

Project.

         There may be multiple ways to allocate costs that implements the Parties’ intent

that all costs are ultimately borne by SB Energy. For example, Ohio Power will have a

retail relationship with SB Energy, and costs allocated to Ohio Power through

Commission-jurisdictional rates can then be further suballocated to SB Energy through

retail rates subject to PUCO’s jurisdiction. While the cost allocation methodology will

ultimately be addressed in a future proceeding, the Commission should make clear at this

early stage of the SAA process that any cost allocation methodology must implement the

Parties’ intent that SB Energy bear the costs of the transmission investment required to

serve the Project. The Commission should ensure that any action it takes in this


24
   Likewise, as PUCO itself has recognized, state commissions lack authority to address how costs are
allocated through Commission-jurisdictional rates. In re Application of Ohio Power Co. for New Tariffs
Related to Data Ctrs. & Mobile Data Ctrs., No. 24-508-EL-ATA, Order ¶ 132 (Pub. Utils. Comm’n of
Ohio July 9, 2025) (explaining that issues concerning “wholesale [cost] impacts” are “statutorily outside of
this Commission’s intrastate purview”).
25
  In contrast, Commission-jurisdictional rates that allocate all costs to Ohio Power could then be further
suballocated to SB Energy, as SB Energy will be a retail customer of Ohio Power, and PUCO has authority
over Ohio Power’s retail rates and retail cost allocation.
                                          -8-


proceeding is consistent with that goal and ensures that other wholesale transmission

customers, such as Buckeye, are not allocated any of the costs associated with the

Project.

                                 CONCLUSION

       Buckeye requests that the Commission give full consideration to these comments

and concerns, and that its action in this proceeding makes clear that other wholesale

transmission customers (such as Buckeye) should not be allocated any of the costs of the

Project.
